_comment_name: HK Grotesk is what this typeface was called before it was renamed,
and it is still the name people ask for it by. It is not the name
the file answers to: the name table inside the file says 'Hanken
Grotesk', and the name table is the only thing Windows and local()
key on. The pack is declared under what the file says; the old name
is written down here so the next person looking for HK Grotesk
_comment_family: The heavy end of the family, and the cut fitness-story picks its
words out in. That pack's block is
hanken-grotesk-extralightitalic — the other end of the same axis, 250
against 800 — so the two are told apart by weight alone, and a face
id typed wrong so that both resolve here is not a different look, it
is the highlight disappearing into the text.
Every cut of this family that the app carries leans, so name ID 1
here ('Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold') names a WEIGHT rather than a cut:
it is a name the upright ExtraBold answers to as well, on a machine
that happens to have it. The full name (ID 4) is what gets declared
instead, the same way telegraf-ultrabold declares 'Telegraf
UltraBold' rather than 'Telegraf'. The typographic family (ID 16) is
the bare 'Hanken Grotesk' on all four cuts, which is the level at
which they really are one family and exactly why no pack may be
declared at it.
Weight 800, which is what the file's OS/2 table says and what the cut
is. Asking for 700 invites a browser to synthesise the difference on
top of a face that already has it.
Registered at style normal, the same way rift and the other Hanken
packs are. The slant is drawn into the letterforms; declaring the
face italic as well would leave the canvas — which asks for normal —
either missing it or being handed a synthetic oblique of something
else. Normal means 'this file, as drawn'.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. Nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file.
The first is the PostScript name and is also what the installer
registers the face under; the second is the Windows full name. Both
name this one cut rather than a weight or a family, so a machine
answering to either is answering with this file — which is exactly
what the fallback route is for. Neither 'Hanken Grotesk' nor 'Hanken
Grotesk ExtraBold' is listed: the first is shared with every other
cut, and the second would let the upright ExtraBold answer.
_comment_stack: The fallbacks are damage limitation and never a design choice — a
title laid out against the wrong metrics is broken, not merely
different, which is what fontguard exists to catch before it is ever
drawn. Not Impact and Arial Black, which is where the display cuts in
this folder fall through to: this is a text grotesque set at caption
size, and Segoe UI Black is both the nearest weight and the nearest
proportion every Windows this app runs on is certain to have.
stack: 'Hanken Grotesk ExtraBold Italic', 'Segoe UI Black', 'Segoe UI', Arial, sans-serif
